glossary.Splenic infarction: Death of spleen tissue from loss of its blood supply.
glossary.Autosomal dominant: Inherited so that one faulty copy of the gene from either parent is enough to cause the condition.
glossary.Pseudomonas aeruginosa: A Gram-negative rod that causes hospital and opportunistic infections and resists many antibiotics.
glossary.Pneumococcal sepsis: Sepsis caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, the classic OPSI organism.
glossary.DVT: Deep vein thrombosis: a blood clot in a deep vein, usually of the leg.
glossary.Pulmonary embolism: A blood clot blocking an artery in the lungs, usually from a DVT.
glossary.Glycosylation: Attachment of glucose to proteins such as haemoglobin; longer-lived red cells collect more.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.Immunisation status: Record of which vaccines a patient has had.
glossary.Elective splenectomy: A planned, non-emergency operation to remove the spleen.
glossary.Antibiotic prophylaxis: Regular antibiotics taken to prevent, rather than treat, infection.
glossary.Influenza vaccine: Yearly flu jab matched to circulating strains.
glossary.Meningococcal type C vaccine: Vaccine protecting against group C Neisseria meningitidis.
glossary.Booster: A repeat vaccine dose to restore fading immunity.
glossary.Mechanical filtration: The spleen physically removing old or abnormal cells and particles as blood passes through.
glossary.Opsonising antibodies: Antibodies that coat bacteria so phagocytes can recognise and engulf them.
glossary.Nuclear remnants: Leftover fragments of DNA inside red cells after the nucleus is expelled.
glossary.Splenic atrophy: Shrinking and scarring of the spleen.
glossary.Functional asplenia: A spleen that is present but no longer works.
glossary.Capsule: A slippery polysaccharide coat around some bacteria that resists phagocytosis.
glossary.Sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated response to infection.
glossary.Haemorrhage: Bleeding, here a surgical risk of splenectomy.
glossary.IV antibiotics: Antibiotics given directly into a vein for fast, reliable levels.
